blockdesc-primitivesieve-*: A copper tier hand crank sieve. Feed it gravel, sand, soil, or any vanilla pannable material and let the shaft do the panning for you. Input from the top or the side facing you; output drops below and out the opposite side, so it sits cleanly on top of a storage. Yield matches hand panning; the saving is your hands.

blockdesc-shaft-*: Carries rotation between machines. Wrap in a frame to pass it through walls and floors.
blockdesc-handcrank-*: Right click to wind. Provides a brief burst of rotation to a small network.
blockdesc-cogwheel-*: Couples two parallel shafts and reverses their direction. Place on the side of a shaft.
blockdesc-largecogwheel-*: Meshes with a small cogwheel on a perpendicular axis to step speed up or down.
blockdesc-gearbox-*: Redirects rotation between any two perpendicular shafts that meet at the corner.
blockdesc-creativemotor-*: Spins forever with no input. Creative use only.
blockdesc-coalmotor-*: Burns coal to spin a connected network. Open the firedoor side to fuel it.
blockdesc-encasedshaft-*: A shaft sleeved in wood so rotation can run through solid blocks.
blockdesc-kineticquern: An auto-quern. Follows the standard machine layout: input from the left side or top, output from the right side or bottom. Grinds vanilla quern recipes and turns rock grit into a finer dust that sieves at higher yield with no dead rolls.
blockdesc-crusher-bronze-*: The driven head of a crusher pair, cast from bronze. Mount above a Crusher Basin and feed it with a shaft. Pulverizes whatever the basin holds. The iron variant crushes 50% faster.
blockdesc-crusher-iron-*: The driven head of a crusher pair, forged from iron plates. Mount above a Crusher Basin and feed it with a shaft. Pulverizes whatever the basin holds. 50% faster than the bronze variant.
blockdesc-crusher-*: The driven head of a crusher pair. Mount above a Crusher Basin and feed it with a shaft. Pulverizes whatever the basin holds.
blockdesc-crusherbasin-*: Holds the item being crushed. Follows the standard machine layout: input from the left side or top, output from the right side or bottom. Crushes raw rock and stones into grit, and graded ore blocks (poor through bountiful) into enriched ore nuggets.
blockdesc-belt-*: Pushes items along while powered. Right click with another belt to chain them. A belt automatically picks up from any machine's output side it runs past, deposits into any machine's input side, and feeds a chest, vessel or other storage placed at its end with no funnel needed. Items stop at any solid block in their path and wait until the exit clears or a side funnel pulls them off. Right click an empty-handed belt to scoop every item on the chain into your inventory.
blockdesc-funnel-copper-*: Pulls from the block directly above it and ejects out the face it is pointed at. To drain a chest or vessel, the funnel must sit BELOW the storage and face the direction you want items to go. Open to set a filter. 16x slower than the iron funnel and has fewer filter slots.
blockdesc-funnel-iron-*: A faster funnel with more filter slots than the copper version. Pulls from the block directly above it and ejects out the face it is pointed at. To drain a chest or vessel, the funnel must sit BELOW the storage and face the direction you want items to go. Open to set a filter.
blockdesc-kineticsieve-*: An auto-sieve. Follows the standard machine layout: input from the left side or top, output from the right side or bottom. Feed it crushed rock (grit or dust), or any vanilla pannable material, to recover sand, ore nuggets and gems. Nuggets must be smelted in a bloomery or forge for usable metal.
blockdesc-kineticsawmill-*: An auto-sawmill. Follows the standard machine layout: input from the left side or top, output from the right side or bottom. Cuts logs into planks, shafts, sticks or cogwheel sections while powered.
blockdesc-kineticpress-*: An organic extractor. Follows the standard machine layout: input from the left side or top, output from the right side or bottom. Squeezes seeds and fruit into oil and juice while powered.
blockdesc-kineticforgepress-*: A fueled metal press. Feed it fuel, metal, and rotation; it heats the workpiece and stamps hot parts such as plates and refined bloom output. A powered bellows beside it improves chamber heat once bellows are added.
blockdesc-kineticbore-*: A heavy industrial drill. Feed it encased shafts and rotation; it descends one block per cycle, leaving a 3x3 shaft behind it.

vkguide-kineticsfordummies-text:
Vintage Kinematics
If it spins, it works. If it doesn't spin, check your shafts.

This guide covers the basics: how power flows, how to redirect and gear it, and how to move items between machines.

The Basics: RPM and SU
Every kinetic network has two numbers. RPM is rotation speed (signed: positive or negative direction). SU is stress, measured as capacity available versus capacity consumed. If consumers want more SU than sources provide, the network overstresses and stops. If two sources try to drive one network at different RPMs, the network conflicts and stops.

Power Sources
VK ships three: the hand crank (rightmouse to spin), the coal motor (feed it coal), and any vanilla mechanical-power network attached directly to a VK shaft. Place a VK shaft next to a vanilla axle, windmill rotor, or angled gear face on the same axis and VK reads its RPM and torque automatically. More sails and more wind mean more SU.

Carrying Power
A line of shafts on the same axis transmits power without ratio change. To turn a corner, use a gearbox: it accepts a shaft input on one face and drives a perpendicular output. To change ratio, mesh a small cogwheel against a large cogwheel: small driving large is a speed-down with more torque headroom; large driving small is a speed-up with less. Cogs sit on the same axis as the shaft they ride; the gear contact happens at the rim.

Item Logistics
A belt runs between two shaft endpoints on the same axis and conveys items along its length. Place a funnel at the input or output: a funnel always pulls from the block directly above it and pushes into the block on the side it is facing (north, east, south, or west). This means you can route items sideways out of a chest into a belt, into a machine's input face, or back into another container, just by aiming the funnel the right way when you place it. Funnels can also sit directly above a belt to drop items onto it, or alongside a belt facing inward to push items onto it. Compatible with vanilla chests, vessels, baskets, and most modded storage blocks. Each funnel has a filter slot with whitelist, blacklist, and fuzzy modes. Iron funnels move items faster than copper.

A belt that ends or runs alongside a machine talks to it the same way a funnel does: items at the belt's exit are pushed straight into the machine's mapped input slot, and a machine's output buffer pushes straight onto an adjacent belt with no funnel needed. Every machine declares which faces are inputs and which are outputs; check each machine's handbook page for the specifics.

Machines
Every machine in VK shares the same IO layout: items go in from the left side or the top, and out from the right side or the bottom. Point a funnel or belt at the correct face and it just works; no per-machine memorization. Each consumer also needs its driving face on the correct shaft axis. Open the GUI to see input, output, and progress.
- Kinetic quern: grinds via vanilla quern recipes.
- Crusher with a basin: crushes ores and rocks; the basin holds output and pushes to adjacent funnels or chests.
- Kinetic sieve: auto-pans gravel, sand, and crushed rock. Uses vanilla panningDrops so any pannable material from other mods works.
- Sawmill: cuts logs into planks and boards.
- Press: produces pressed goods with a fluid buffer.
- Kinetic bore: multi-block drill that descends through stone and retracts on demand.
- Kinetic igniter: spark source for fueled blocks.

Your First Build
Start small: a hand crank driving a primitive sieve through a single shaft. Wind the crank, watch the sieve work. Then experiment with gearing: mesh a small cogwheel against a large cogwheel between the crank and the sieve. Try both directions: small driving large, then large driving small. See how fast you can make the sieve run before something gives. This is the whole mod in miniature: a source, a shaft, a gear stage, a consumer. Every later build is just more of the same.

Troubleshooting
Check the in-world tooltip on any shaft or machine for the live RPM and SU readout. If a machine sits idle, look at that readout first.
- Overstressed: SU demand exceeds capacity. Add another source, remove a consumer, or gear down to lower the RPM (consumer SU scales with RPM).
- Conflicted: two sources are pushing different RPMs into the same network. Disconnect one, or split the line with a vanilla clutch or brake.
- RPM zero, no overstress: a shaft segment is broken between source and consumer, or the source itself is stopped (low wind, no fuel, idle crank).

Build small, test as you go, and grow outward from a known-working source.
